nodes.description: Public mapping(address => uint256) tracking token balances of each account.
Public string token name set to EGYPT_WINS.
Public string token symbol set to EGYWII.
Public uint8 number of decimals set to 18.
Public uint256 total token supply minted to the deployer.
Public nested mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) of spending approvals.
Constructor-like function that mints totalSupply to msg.sender and emits Transfer.
Public function moving value tokens from msg.sender to to, with a balance require check.
Public function setting allowance[msg.sender][spender] = value and emitting Approval.
Public function moving value tokens from from to to using and decrementing allowance.
Caller-controlled address used as balance owner, allowance owner and initial supply recipient.
balanceOf[msg.sender] -= value unchecked subtraction inside transfer.
balanceOf[to] += value unchecked addition inside transfer.
balanceOf[from] -= value unchecked subtraction inside transferFrom.
balanceOf[to] += value unchecked addition inside transferFrom.
allowance[from][msg.sender] -= value unchecked subtraction inside transferFrom.
allowance[msg.sender][spender] = value state write inside approve, with no zero-first protection.
Recipient address parameter of transfer.
Amount parameter of transfer.
Spender address parameter of approve.
Approval amount parameter of approve.
Source address parameter of transferFrom.
Destination address parameter of transferFrom.
Amount parameter of transferFrom.

edges.reason: totalSupply is read by the constructor to initialize balances.
msg.sender is the unrestricted recipient of the whole initial supply.
msg.sender selects which balance is debited in transfer.
msg.sender is the owner key when writing allowance in approve.
msg.sender is the spender key used in transferFrom allowance checks.
transfer executes the unchecked subtraction on the sender balance.
transfer executes the unchecked addition on the recipient balance.
balanceOf is read to validate and compute the new sender balance.
The decremented sender balance is written back into balanceOf.
The value parameter is subtracted from the sender balance.
msg.sender determines the storage slot being decremented.
The value parameter is added to the recipient balance.
The to parameter determines the recipient storage slot being credited.
The incremented recipient balance is written back into balanceOf.
The to parameter is an input of transfer.
The value parameter is an input of transfer.
The spender parameter is an input of approve.
The value parameter is an input of approve.
approve performs the allowance state write.
allowance mapping is read and updated by the approve write.
The new allowance value is stored back into the allowance mapping.
transferFrom executes the unchecked subtraction on the from balance.
transferFrom executes the unchecked addition on the to balance.
transferFrom executes the unchecked subtraction on the allowance.
The from parameter is an input of transferFrom.
The to parameter is an input of transferFrom.
The value parameter is an input of transferFrom.
The from parameter selects the balance slot being decremented.
balanceOf[from] is checked then decremented in transferFrom.
The decremented from balance is written back into balanceOf.
The to parameter selects the balance slot being credited.
The incremented to balance is written back into balanceOf.
The value parameter is subtracted from the allowance.
The from parameter is part of the allowance lookup key.
msg.sender is the spender key of the allowance being decremented.
allowance[from][msg.sender] is checked and decremented.
The decremented allowance is written back into the allowance mapping.

normalization_plan.reason: The to parameter is only meaningful as an argument of transfer and should be merged into its function.
The value parameter directly feeds the unchecked balance subtraction inside transfer.
The spender parameter is only used as a key for the approve allowance write and merges into approve.
The value parameter is the stored approval amount and merges into approve.
The from parameter is only meaningful as an argument of transferFrom and merges into its function.
The to parameter is only meaningful as an argument of transferFrom and merges into its function.
The value parameter directly feeds the unchecked balance and allowance subtractions in transferFrom.
